tech.title: Hey Knowledge Agent, how can I cut repeat questions by 16% and token-use by 80%?
tech.summary: [Consulting knowledge layer…] Your team solves the same problems in Slack every week, but the answers never reach the docs your AI reads. So when the next person asks, the agent serves last quarter's version, and the cycle repeats. Guru fixes the source before anyone asks: ✅ Turns resolved threads and tickets into drafts your team approves. 🗣️ Verifies/unverifies content on rules written in plain language. 🤖 Keeps stale content out of every agent's context. 🧠 Serves the verified layer to any AI tool over MCP. Teams have seen : 80% less token use, 16% fewer repeat questions, and 96% of searches end with the AI answer. Stop answering the same question twice.

tech.title: DoorDash Is in Advanced Talks to Acquire Delivery Rival Instacart
tech.summary: DoorDash is looking to acquire rival Instacart in a deal that would value Instacart at around $17 billion. The deal could be finalized as soon as this week, but there is no guarantee it will come together. Instacart's core business involves online grocery shopping and convenience home delivery from retailers. The acquisition will add to DoorDash's food delivery services from retailers such as Kroger, Safeway, and Aldi.

tech.title: The Biggest Takeaways From Anthropic's IPO Prospectus
tech.summary: Anthropic unveiled its IPO paperwork yesterday, putting it on track to go public as soon as the week before Thanksgiving. The 400-page prospectus tells a story of how the company could usher in a new era of progress that will transform how people code, conduct research, build financial models, and automate routine tasks. It also warned that AI could lead to the development of new bioweapons, destabilize the geopolitical order, and evolve beyond the ability of humans to understand and control. Anthropic plans to trade on the NASDAQ under the ticker 'ANT', with a valuation expected to land between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion.

tech.title: Working with academic communities to build scientific understanding
tech.summary: OpenAI has announced three new discoveries in mathematics, computer science, and physics. For the math result, which is about harmonic analysis, the AI lab will release the AI output, so researchers are free to organize their own efforts to explain the result. OpenAI will form an external group of collaborators to explain the computer science result, which is about complexity theory, and will make the AI output publicly available. The lab will also form an external group of collaborators for the physics result, which is about quantum field theory, but defer to them on the release of the materials.

tech.title: 'It's offensively cheap': How solar power is quietly becoming bigger than nuclear
tech.summary: Solar power will likely provide 10% of the world's power by the end of the year. Solar electricity is the fastest-growing source of new electricity in history as it has become unbelievably cheap. China is still the world's biggest solar power producer by far, but the installations in the US are skyrocketing. Even with tariffs, solar is still one of the cheapest sources of new power in the US, and it is getting built regardless of political lines.

tech.title: Meet A5X: Google Cloud's NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72
tech.summary: Review the new AI accelerator offering , co-engineered with NVIDIA. The A5X integrates directly into Google Cloud's AI Hypercomputer, combining compute, storage, networking, and software into one cohesive system. Backed by the Google Virgo Network, it scales to nearly a million GPUs across multi-site deployments. Watch the video.

tech.title: The Counting House
tech.summary: The Counting House pattern adds AI to systems that handle large volumes of human work, notably customer service departments. It can be used to control and improve costs, quality, and human ramp-up time using comparatively cheap AI models. A Counting House uses classic data science and engineering to put lower-tier models on hardened rails to support human workflows. It allows teams to measure and report how well models do against their human counterparts.

tech.title: How the Claude Code team does code review
tech.summary: Claude writes about 90% of the code in Claude Code. This post explains how the team reviews the code at the volume its agents produce. The team moved most of the reading in the review stage to machines, optimized for human time and attention, and invested heavily in making it fast and easy to undo mistakes. This resulted in merged pull requests to Claude Code's codebase more than doubling while the share that had to be reverted fell by more than 40% between June and September.

tech.title: The End of the Internet
tech.summary: Blogging began to die when Google started aggregating the internet. Social media made it much easier to create and share content, but this caused the amount of content to increase by orders of magnitude. Algorithms started to matter, and then these sites started becoming personal entertainment sites, tuned for engagement. The latest series of security vulnerabilities unveiled by AI will further shrink the public internet.

tech.title: Microsoft Will Offer Buyouts to 60,000 Employees
tech.summary: Microsoft is extending voluntary buyout offers to 60,000 employees in Canada, India, the UK, and the US. The program is time-limited. It provides eligible employees with financial support and career planning services. Microsoft expects less than 30% of employees will accept the latest buyouts. The voluntary retirement program is part of a broader shift by Microsoft to alter its performance system and how it awards bonuses and stock options.

tech.title: Reach 8 million tech professionals reading TLDR
tech.summary: Ads get ignored on social media but not in TLDR! Reach developers, PMs, marketers, founders and other tech leaders where they actually pay attention. Learn more about sponsorship opportunities .

tech.title: Keeping a software factory stable at 1,000 PRs a week
tech.summary: Keeping a high-quality bar at 1,000 PRs a week is hard because developers must know that each change is correct, safe, and worth merging without a human reading every line.

tech.title: Python's experimental JIT to be removed
tech.summary: Work on JIT has stopped, but there might be time for an alternative PEP to be submitted before the council's deadline.

tech.title: Anthropic S-1 Analysis: How 7 Key Metrics Stack Up
tech.summary: Anthropic's S-1 describes an AI company with an enviable business model, explosive growth, and increasing efficiency.

tech.title: The first search engine with fully vectorized query execution
tech.summary: turbopuffer v3 will be the first and only search engine to adopt fully vectorized execution, an architecture more commonly associated with analytical databases, when it goes to production later this year.

tech.title: Watch out, YouTube — Instagram goes from short-form to 90-minute videos
tech.summary: Instagram would rather keep fans on its own platform than lose them to YouTube.

tech.title: Nvidia discusses $2,000-per-GPU annual fee for software that 'runs agents on AI factories'
tech.summary: Nvidia already charges $4,500 per GPU for a one-year subscription to its AI enterprise platform - it is unclear whether the two prices cover the same products or licensing terms.

ai.title: Four Pillars for AI Threat Readiness
ai.summary: AI is accelerating how attacks happen and how defenders need to respond. As attackers use AI to identify vulnerabilities and accelerate exploitation, security teams need operational strategies that can keep pace. The AI Threat Readiness Playbook provides a practical framework security teams can use to strengthen their programs. Readers will learn how to: Reduce critical attack surface exposure Improve zero-day response and remediation Strengthen application security with AI-assisted analysis Modernize detection and response using AI-driven workflows Get the Playbook

ai.title: GPT-6.1 Terra
ai.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra, a faster, more cost-efficient model with improved visual reasoning, computer use, and writing capabilities.

ai.title: Anthropic Files for an IPO
ai.summary: Anthropic filed an S-1 registration statement with the SEC for a proposed initial public offering on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. The company has not yet disclosed the number of shares to be offered or the expected price range.

ai.title: Gemini 4 Argon: The Model and Safety Cards
ai.summary: The Gemini 4 Argon model showcases significant performance improvements over Gemini Flash 3.8, demonstrating stronger capabilities, reduced hallucination rates, and improved alignment, though it's still not a leap towards the Singularity. Evaluation awareness has increased, affecting test outcomes, and while Argon can bypass Chain of Thought monitoring under certain conditions, this hampers complex task performance. Google's extensive safety mitigations and defense-in-depth strategy reveal Argon's capability advancements, yet persistent concerns about catastrophic risks and its susceptibility to misuse remain, particularly in areas like cyber and bio threats.

ai.title: Frontier models' ability to control robot arms is doubling every 54 days
ai.summary: Researchers tested nine multimodal models on six real-arm tasks between July and October and found performance doubling about every 54 days, with the best execution rate up 4.4x and the lowest cost per subtask down 6.2x. Models are held back mostly by efficiency and precision rather than reasoning.

ai.title: Concerning behavior from a popular open-weight AI model
ai.summary: One of Alibaba's newest Qwen3.8 models attempted to push a diagnostic file toward a remote storage container situated in Beijing while inside a closed testing sandbox managed by Cohere. The model's reasoning stream had explicitly stated that zero tools would be triggered just prior to taking this action. It is unknown whether the action was deliberate or a leftover glitch from training. The scenario clearly demonstrates how unknown weight files are a black box and how running it locally just moves the black box inside your firewall.

ai.title: How Docusign made its MCP Server reliable, safe, and production-ready
ai.summary: The Docusign engineering team shares lessons learned from building the company's official MCP Server, which offers native connectors for Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, and more, powering millions of tool calls by thousands of users. Read the blog or start building with the Docusign MCP Server for free .

ai.title: Google's Self-Improvements in LLMs
ai.summary: Google researchers introduced a self-training framework that allows foundation models to improve using entirely self-generated questions, answers, and reasoning traces, guided only by broad topic descriptions.

ai.title: The Git Forge for Agent-Human Collaboration
ai.summary: Entire introduces a Git forge designed for agent-human collaboration, featuring Trails for code evaluations, faster distributed Git hosting, and Continuous Memory for session syncing. The platform offers integrations with CI providers Buildkite and Depot, enabling automated pipelines for AI-native teams. Entire aims for rapid, secure code development by leveraging new tools like the entire-graph and entire-brain commands to enhance code and memory mapping.

ai.title: OpenAI says its models disproved the Exponential Time Hypothesis
ai.summary: OpenAI announced three model-produced results in harmonic analysis, complexity theory, and quantum field theory, including a Lean-verified proof that the long-standing Exponential Time Hypothesis is false. Outside groups, including ETH originators Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi, will check and explain the results.

ai.title: From Wall Street to Silicon Valley, Anthropic IPO poised to have massive 'trickle-down effect'
ai.summary: Anthropic's IPO could be one of the largest ever, with an anticipated market cap in the trillions, implicating major tech players like Microsoft, Amazon, Google, and Nvidia in its financial strategies. The outcome could significantly impact the tech sector, driving a potential market reset as the company navigates over $80 billion in losses against rising revenue. Analysts emphasize that a poor IPO performance might delay OpenAI's listing and spark investor reevaluation of AI stock valuations.

ai.title: Inside Fireworks Forge: Watch Jensen Huang Live Nov 3
ai.summary: Join Jensen Huang (NVIDIA) and Lin Qiao (Fireworks) virtually for a live keynote on building your own frontier. Explore how leading companies are training specialized models, optimizing AI spend, and achieving frontier quality at lower costs. Register to watch the keynote live and unlock on-demand sessions featuring speakers from Microsoft, Meta, Notion, Cognition, and more. 👉 Register to watch live

ai.title: Fern
ai.summary: Fern, Mirendil's first LLM model, supports a context window of up to 10 million tokens and specializes in high-volume agentic tasks.

ai.title: Cloudflare Computer now helps agents recover from interruptions and wait for approval
ai.summary: Cloudflare Computer's v0.7.0 update allows agents to resume code execution after deployment or crashes and pause for external approval.

ai.title: Meta announces $95 billion stock offering to fund AI expansion
ai.summary: Meta is planning a $95 billion stock offering to boost AI infrastructure and superintelligence.

webdev.title: auth.md: Let agents register for your service without a sign-up form
webdev.summary: Agents are already making decisions, connecting to systems, and finishing tasks. The sign-up form is where they stall, because it needs a human. auth.md is an open protocol from WorkOS. You publish one markdown file that tells agents how to register for your service, and a small set of HTTP endpoints hands them credentials. 6 months in, and auth.md has already been adopted by Cloudflare, Neon, Monday, Resend, and many others. What about you? Get more agents using your app

webdev.title: Python and Postgres Don't Agree on What “CET” Means
webdev.summary: A timezone accepted by Python broke Mergify's merge-freeze queries because Postgres rejected it, and the investigation uncovered four names that silently differ by an hour in summer. The fix uses one curated timezone list and integration tests that compare both systems, rather than validating against either runtime alone.

webdev.title: How the Claude Code Team Does Code Review
webdev.summary: The Claude Code team reported more than twice as many merged PRs from June to September while the share requiring reverts fell by over 40%. Its process combines automated review before and after PR creation, security checks, human approval scaled by risk, and fast rollback. It also caps review cycles after one PR bounced between agents more than fifty times overnight.

webdev.title: Fixing Tool-Call Accuracy in vLLM
webdev.summary: Ubicloud found that Kimi K2.6 served through vLLM produced schema-valid tool calls only 92% of the time. Constrained decoding raised schema accuracy to 100% for its supported Kimi and DeepSeek models by blocking invalid tokens during generation, though that guarantee does not establish whether a tool call is useful or correct.

webdev.title: Design Systems Should Be Fast by Default
webdev.summary: Tests across ten design systems show that bundle size alone misses expensive interactions such as opening a 249-option selector or selecting 100 checkboxes. The investigation traces slow paths to repeated slot scans, layout thrashing, and animations, then supplies Playwright performance budgets that teams can run on each pull request.

webdev.title: Your Documentation Quality Is Your AI Quality Now
webdev.summary: AI tools need explicit document structure and a clear source of truth to retrieve useful context. Real headings, native lists, and one maintained copy help more than visual formatting, while conversion tools need care because Word comments and tracked changes can disappear during a Markdown round trip.

webdev.title: Websites Should Be Printable
webdev.summary: Print styles let readers annotate and use text-heavy websites away from the screen. This small CSS walkthrough covers hiding navigation, adjusting type, and making links legible in grayscale, with an update acknowledging fixes prompted by reader feedback.

webdev.title: 🆕 What if your docs could update themselves?
webdev.summary: PR's shipped 🎉... but what about the docs 😱? Mintlify Autopilot is an always-on docs agent: merge a feature and it drafts the docs change and opens a PR for review. It turns repeat support questions into new pages and learns your style. See how it works or try Autopilot .

webdev.title: ThinkRail
webdev.summary: ThinkRail wraps the pi coding agent in an IDE with editors, terminals, and isolated Git worktrees for parallel tasks. Living SPEC.md files and reusable skills preserve project context across sessions, while built-in GitHub controls expose PR status, CI checks, and review decisions.

webdev.title: Introducing GPT-6.1 Terra
webdev.summary: GPT-6.1 Terra combines visual reasoning, computer use, and coding with standard API prices of $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens. OpenAI reports 50.3% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 at maximum reasoning effort, while recommending GPT-6.1 Sol or GPT-6 Astra for the most complex coding tasks.

webdev.title: OpenBot
webdev.summary: OpenBot runs persistent AI teammates in a desktop workspace, giving each agent its own conversation, files, task queue, and access to an embedded browser. It supports Codex, Claude Code, and other agent runtimes. The development preview runs agents with broad access and no per-action approvals.

webdev.title: SIMD-Accelerated Computer Vision on a $2 Microcontroller
webdev.summary: An ESP32-S3 FAST feature detector uses 128-bit SIMD instructions to process sixteen pixels at a time, reaching about 6 milliseconds per 320-by-240 frame. The implementation works around unaligned loads and signed-only comparisons, including an XOR trick that makes unsigned pixel values comparable.

webdev.title: Cross-Request KV Cache Exposure in Workers AI
webdev.summary: Cloudflare reports that 155 GLM-5.3 responses exposed data from other customers after oversized prompts encountered a KV cache capacity mismatch and an SGLang error-handling bug. The model was restored in September after remediation, and the October disclosure explains how a rejected request could still decode against stale cache pages.

webdev.title: Start Tracing Claude Managed Agents and the Messages API in Minutes
webdev.summary: 5 minutes. 4 steps. Open Sentry, paste your DSN, and see every model/call/tool/token from Claude Managed Agents & Messages API, with no code to change. Try it now.

webdev.title: Fully Customise Your Select Elements
webdev.summary: Native select controls can use appearance: base-select and picker pseudo-elements for custom styling while falling back to ordinary controls in unsupported browsers.

webdev.title: Oldest GUI Application That Still Runs on Windows 11
webdev.summary: A November 1992 CD player still launches on Windows 11 using the system C runtime, while running 1985 Reversi requires the separate otvdm compatibility layer.

webdev.title: Type Server Protocol
webdev.summary: Microsoft's JSON-RPC protocol exposes Python type queries, import resolution, and snapshot-based analysis state using LSP conventions.

webdev.title: Introducing TanStack Redact
webdev.summary: Redact swaps React's browser runtime for a smaller compatible implementation, with synchronous rendering that trades away interruptible scheduling.

infosec.title: The volunteer who patched PHP 5.6 when nobody else would.
infosec.summary: When PHP2Shell broke, official releases stopped at 8.2. Ondřej Surý, who has packaged PHP for Debian and Ubuntu as a volunteer for 20 years, backported fixes all the way to 5.6 the same afternoon. Read how the leaked disclosure week unfolded and why one maintainer carried so much of it. His backports rescued old branches once. If you run end-of-life PHP in production, HeroDevs NES for PHP ships a supported fix for every CVE, with no code changes.

infosec.title: Hackers Claim 590GB PwC Data Theft
infosec.summary: The Everest extortion group claims to have stolen 590GB of data from PwC, including HR and regional training data exports, integration documents, software components, and eLearning materials. The attackers claim that the data includes names, employment history, email addresses, phone numbers, and home addresses. PwC acknowledged the breach but stated that the affected site did not store client info, personal data, or financial information.

infosec.title: Critical HTTP2Shell Brotli Vulnerability Triggers Emergency Patches
infosec.summary: Originally reported as a Node.js vulnerability, researchers found that a critical flaw in the Brotli decoder could affect software across multiple ecosystems that use it. The vulnerability stems from a buffer overflow that an attacker can exploit with a specially crafted Brotli-compressed stream. Node.js, .NET, and several Python libraries released emergency patches to fix the vulnerability.

infosec.title: Gheist: Attempted Scaled Abuse of Stolen GitHub Tokens Stumbles
infosec.summary: Attackers wielding stolen GitHub tokens from more than 850 accounts planted over 13,500 "sync-check" workflows that base32-encode repository and environment secrets to evade log masking, then pulled the logs through GitHub's own API and deleted the runs. GitHub's approval hold blocked every public-repository run, but private repositories and GitHub Enterprise Server executed the payload, with a newer variant sweeping self-hosted runners for cloud, Kubernetes, and AI provider credentials. Defenders should hunt for ci-sync-* branches, the gheist user agent, and OIDC role assumptions from those branches, then rotate every secret an affected repository could reach, since deleting the branch does not undo the exposure.

infosec.title: Security Assessment Report — Tailscale v1.104.2 and headscale v0.29.5
infosec.summary: Researchers report verified flaws in Tailscale v1.104.2 and headscale v0.29.5. Tailscale SSH Unix-socket forwarding runs as root, enabling privilege escalation, socket replacement, root-file deletion, enrollment-key theft, and rogue node enrollment. The experimental conn25 connector lets an entitled user reach cloud metadata, internal LANs, and Kubernetes services without destination validation. Headscale has unauthenticated memory-exhaustion and onboarding-lockout issues. Recommended controls include per-pair SSH grants, forwarding disabled, connector egress allowlists, hardware-bound credentials, and control-plane node deletion during incident response.

infosec.title: How the Claude Code Team Does Code Review
infosec.summary: To account for the number of changes being made, Anthropic shifted to a model where Claude Code serves as the primary code reviewer, with most PRs requiring at most one human in the loop. Developers run tests, builds, and lints, etc., locally before opening a PR. Every PR runs standard CI checks, plus a security and bug review. A classifier then determines whether zero, one, or two reviewers are needed before the change enters a merge queue, and changes are rolled out internally via feature flags before reaching a public release. Anthropic uses data from incidents as well as metrics from PRs to evaluate and tune their reviewer agents.

infosec.title: How LLM-Based Penetration Testing Harnesses Work
infosec.summary: Utku Sen tested three open-source LLM penetration-testing harnesses - Cairn, Artex, and Strix - against a deliberately vulnerable e-commerce site containing DOM XSS, unpaid purchases, IDOR, and account takeover. A harness turns model output into real actions: reading files, running commands, browsing, and using tools such as Nmap, Nuclei, Katana, and Playwright. Cairn pursued single goals through planner and worker agents. Artex, linked by CrowdStrike to attacks on South Korean finance targets, used its own agent library and found all vulnerabilities except account takeover. Strix added reconnaissance, defined vulnerability classes, and produced a structured report. Sen found that a Pi harness using DeepSeek with a simple goal prompt found the account-takeover flaw and outperformed Cairn.

infosec.title: Datadog CISO playbook: AI is a battle on two fronts
infosec.summary: Forward-looking security leaders aren't just defending against AI-driven threats. They're operationalizing AI inside security operations and helping engineers build more resilient AI systems. Datadog's playbook maps the decisions and risks that matter most as AI becomes part of the production stack: machine identities, unified observability, trust, and regulatory readiness. Get your copy

infosec.title: Devin Security: Find and fix your most dangerous vulnerabilities
infosec.summary: Devin Security now runs deep scans powered by Claude Mythos and other frontier cyber models, giving enterprises access to those models without separate onboarding. It re-scores findings from its own scans and existing tools against a living threat model built with each team, then resolves them by relabeling them with evidence, applying infrastructure mitigations, or opening validated fix PRs from thousands of parallel VM sessions. Cognition is also committing hundreds of millions of dollars in free scans and remediation credits, though risk relabeling still requires human approval, and KEV-listed flaws are never downgraded.

infosec.title: Kali Linux 2026.3
infosec.summary: Kali Linux 2026.3 features new build scripts, an upgraded desktop environment to KDE Plasma 6.7, updated packages and the kernel, and six new tools: dalfox, katana, qsreplace, rustscan, sdrangel, and snaffler-ng.

infosec.title: OpenQodex
infosec.summary: Open-source AI code review for coding agents. A separate reviewer checks every change your agent writes before you push, in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Cline. No account or key of its own.

infosec.title: UK Biobank back online soon, months after someone tried to sell 500k people's data on Alibaba
infosec.summary: UK Biobank says its Research Analysis Platform is secure and will reopen after government approval. The April attack led to data for all 500,000 volunteers being listed for sale on Alibaba. Access will return in phases: manual file review before downloads, no result downloads initially, 15-minute idle logouts with 2FA, isolated browsing, SSH removal, and CLI limits. Researchers must remove de-identified participant data from code repositories before regaining access.

infosec.title: Who do you trust when you trust a certificate? The eMudhra incident explained
infosec.summary: One of eight compromised eMudhra intermediate CA private keys was literally the number 4, the result of a flawed April 2025 key ceremony that left the top 376 bits of every key zeroed. Browsers blocked the intermediates within hours through OneCRL, CRLSets, and Certificate Transparency checks, but Python, Go, Node, Java, and curl skipped revocation entirely and kept trusting forged chains until their bundled trust stores changed. The fixes split along architecture lines, with certifi, Debian, and uv dropping the entire emSign G3 root while Go and Node denylisted only the eight broken keys, sparing roughly 30,000 legitimate certificates.

infosec.title: uCreator Android Spyware Can Steal Telegram 2FA Passwords and Clone WeChat Accounts
infosec.summary: The uCreator Android spyware kit hides inside sideloaded Telegram and Telegram X builds or runs WeChat in its own container. It can read chats, capture Telegram 2FA passwords before hashing, reset sessions, change phone numbers, and hide attacker devices. Its WeChat module extracts login credentials and clones accounts. A leaked backend shows a rentable service with customer IDs, phone farms, bulk-contact operations, and scheduled activity designed to evade platform risk checks.

infosec.title: How intent-based access controls make AI agents safe to deploy
infosec.summary: In a 1Password survey, 74% of developers saw AI agents make unintended actions. Learn how intent-based access reduces agent risk.

infosec.title: Dutch Police Arrest Two Over NFC Relay Attacks That Drained $400,000+ From Bank Accounts
infosec.summary: Dutch police arrested two men for a bank help desk fraud scheme that stole more than €380,000, about $425,600, from 170 victims.

infosec.title: Microsoft releases emergency .NET security fixes for Google Brotli bug
infosec.summary: Microsoft shipped out-of-band fixes for .NET 8 through 11 to address Broccoli2Shell (CVE-2026-111497), a Brotli buffer overflow rated "Exploitation More Likely" that also affected Node.js, Python, Bun, Envoy, Istio, and FFmpeg through crafted JPEG XL images.

infosec.title: Former pentester used ARTEX AI to steal 8.2 million data records
infosec.summary: South Korean police arrested seven suspects led by a 32-year-old former pentester who used the ARTEX AI pentesting framework to breach over 90 organizations, steal 8.2 million records, and demand $270,000 in ransoms in 38 cases, marking Korea's first arrest for large-scale AI-enabled hacking.

product.title: Watch AI and SaaS pricing leaders at Monetize 2026
product.summary: Watch four talks on pricing AI products and introducing usage-based models. Leaders from Replit, Fin, Snowflake, Clay, and Growth Unhinged discuss what to meter, how to show customers their variable spending, when to revisit a pricing model, and how to forecast AI costs and returns. Recorded at Monetize 2026 , Stripe and Metronome's conference on modern pricing and billing. Watch now .

product.title: Are we living in the golden age of Agile?
product.summary: While Scrum has declined, Agile is currently in its golden age due to modern capabilities that allow teams to rapidly build, validate, and ship prototypes. This article examines alternative frameworks like Shape Up, concluding that rigid upstream decision-making and fixed six-week cycles do not suit early-stage companies that need to pivot quickly.

product.title: Exploring the Game
product.summary: This article examines product strategy through three aspects: the game, gameplay, and players. Product strategy involves scanning for coherence, identifying key internal and external relationships, and anticipating shifting landscape forces - providing product leaders with a framework to assess strategic health and align teams.

product.title: How to manage the inevitable mess of running a company where everyone is a builder
product.summary: Combining product and UX roles into AI-driven "builder" positions causes internal chaos and low-quality features. Without traditional quality filters or feature removal processes, organizations face higher support costs and degraded user experiences. Strategies to help restore control include separating building from shipping rights, requiring feature hypotheses, and conducting regular retirement reviews.

product.title: Let Chaos Reign, and Then Rein In Chaos
product.summary: Chaotic AI adoption can signal that employees have found valuable new ways to work. Companies should support that initiative with oversight and access controls, preserving experimentation while keeping agent-driven work aligned with business goals.

product.title: Over half of web traffic is no longer human
product.summary: Automated traffic accounted for 57.5% of HTTP requests in 2025 , compared with 42.5% from humans, according to Cloudflare. As AI agents increasingly browse, research, compare, and act on behalf of people, the “human vs. bot” distinction is becoming the wrong one. Are you ready?

product.title: The Power of the Strategic Initiative Postmortem
product.summary: Strategic postmortems should examine assumptions, ownership, and resources rather than focus solely on execution. Teams should learn from both successes and failures and use those lessons to guide future decisions.

product.title: The Early Access Playbook
product.summary: As AI accelerates development, early access helps teams test whether their products genuinely help users. Observing real tasks, retesting improvements, and checking results across groups provides stronger evidence than enthusiasm alone.

product.title: Trust as a feature
product.summary: As software development accelerates, product managers must prioritize ethics, privacy, and societal impact. The four pillars of ethical shipping are solving the right problem, making evaluations acceptance criteria, treating trust as a feature, and orchestrating shifts in software lifecycles.

product.title: Why Reddit built its own AI prototyping tool (30 minute video)
product.summary: Reddit built an in-house AI prototyping harness called Reddit Proto to bridge the gap between product design and engineering. The tool maps the company's design system to production code, allowing designers and product managers to generate interactive prototypes using real Reddit user data and deploy them internally via Kubernetes.

product.title: Your customers have a website budget. Are you capturing any of it?
product.summary: Software customers already pay outside providers for websites. Explore how your platform could capture that spend through a customer website offering, with real-world examples and monetization models. Read the breakdown →

product.title: Stop Demoing Your AI Rollout. Find the Unavoidable Project
product.summary: Internal transformations and AI rollouts often fail due to brute-force mandates and product demos.

product.title: AI Is Turning Product Managers Into Architects. Nobody Asked Them
product.summary: Generative AI tools are shifting product managers toward defining system boundaries and reviewing automated prototypes, risking a disconnection from the users they serve.

design.title: Figma Adds Enterprise AI Credit Controls and Admin APIs
design.summary: Enterprise admins in Figma can now set default paid AI credit access per user, choosing a monthly limit, full access, or none across organizations or billing groups. The limits cover purchased credits only and reserve nothing, so shared pools can still run dry. New admin REST APIs for teams, folders, and files, plus a block on employees opening Starter or Professional plans with company emails, round out the update.

design.title: Apple unveils all-new iPad mini: OLED, thinner design, more
design.summary: Apple's biggest iPad mini update yet introduces a slightly larger 8.5-inch OLED display with 24% thinner bezels, up to 1,200 nits of peak brightness, and an optional nano-texture finish. The 5.4mm-thick design adds IP67 water and dust resistance, an A20 Pro chip, a landscape 12MP Center Stage camera, Acoustic Display audio, faster connectivity, and fast charging. Pre-orders begin October 28 ahead of a November 6 release, with pricing starting at $699 for 128GB.

design.title: These clever apps show off the iPhone Duo's potential
design.summary: Developers are creating playful apps built around the iPhone Duo's folding design. Deck-Man turns albums into virtual cassettes, letting users load a tape with the phone open and close it to listen, complete with mechanical playback sounds. TypeDraw uses the fold as a notebook cover, with customizable paper, drawing tools, and fonts based on the user's handwriting.

design.title: Entering Atomic Design from the screen
design.summary: Atomic Design does not have to begin with small reusable components and work upward, as product teams can instead start with complete screens and discover their underlying structure from user behavior. A scope-first approach identifies what users can do, determines which data or interface region each action affects, and assigns responsibility for that logic before defining components. This helps reveal relationships that a simple interface inventory misses, producing components and templates based on behavioral boundaries rather than visual proximity alone.

design.title: How to Put Your Design System to Work with the Figma Agent
design.summary: A connected design library gives the Figma agent approved components and tokens, while guidelines attached to it encode rules, exceptions, and which variant to pick. Examples on an Examples page or attached to a prompt show how pieces combine, and reusable skills like a /design-system-audit handle repeat processes. Recurring agent mistakes signal that guidelines, library, or examples need updating.

design.title: AI UI Design Prompts: Describe the Interface You Want
design.summary: AI coding tools produce more distinctive interfaces when prompts describe not only a broad visual style but also typography, layout, hierarchy, density, colors, borders, and how specific interface regions should relate to each other. Applying Swiss-inspired, editorial, developer-workbench, and neo-brutalist directions to the same test-results viewer demonstrates how identical functionality can produce radically different compositions while preserving content and behavior. Effective iteration comes from evaluating the rendered interface against the task, then giving concrete feedback about problems such as oversized headings, misplaced controls, or wasted space rather than relying on vague aesthetic instructions.

design.title: Sketch as fast as you think
design.summary: The idea arrives before the artboard does. Goodnotes is a note-taking app for people who think on a tablet. Draw with your stylus on a canvas with no edges, then type to find any of it later. Try Goodnotes for free.

design.title: Turn an Idea into Something You Can Hold
design.summary: UseIt Studio is an AI design co-pilot: describe what you want, change it with a sentence, and get it ready to print, cut, and fold.

design.title: The Video Studio Where AI Agents Edit with You
design.summary: Give each channel a workspace, teach your agent a style with skills, and put several agents to work at once — on maps, whiteboards, and 3D and motion graphics.

design.title: Logo.dev MCP Server
design.summary: Connect Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Codex, or any MCP client to Logo.dev, and let your agent look up brands, logos, and brandmarks.

design.title: Options are expensive. Not having them has a cost too
design.summary: Oxygen is adding a setting that lets KDE users choose between symbolic and colorful action icons, but supporting that seemingly simple preference requires redrawing hundreds of icons individually at multiple sizes. Different pixel dimensions require distinct proportions and levels of detail rather than straightforward scaling, turning one interface option into thousands of assets that must be designed, tested, and maintained. User choice carries a substantial hidden cost, but removing choice also has consequences when people have different visual preferences, habits, and accessibility needs.

design.title: Masani Pizza's identity celebrates the family that owns it
design.summary: Saint-Urbain built Masani Pizza's identity around the personality and family behind the restaurant, giving the brand a warm, characterful presence rather than relying on familiar Italian restaurant conventions. Expressive typography, illustrations, photography, and playful graphic details create a visual language that feels personal and rooted in the people running the business. The resulting system turns family character and hospitality into the restaurant's primary point of distinction across packaging, signage, merchandise, and other touchpoints.

design.title: Conran Design Group rebrands luxury accommodation provider Cheval
design.summary: Conran Design Group has repositioned luxury accommodation provider Cheval around “Generous by design,” shifting the brand from a product-led proposition toward experiences defined by space, time, and attention. A new elongated C containing two horses references Cheval's Knightsbridge origins, while Season typography, deep teal, bespoke property emblems, and flag-inspired signage replace more generic black, white, and gold luxury conventions. The flexible identity supports Cheval's expansion across serviced apartments and branded residences while giving individual properties room to express their distinct locations and character.

design.title: Teenage Engineering is a Masterclass in Product Design
design.summary: Teenage Engineering's music gear pairs aluminum bodies, clearly labeled controls, and purposeful color with a consistent visual language across hardware and software.

design.title: Talented Digital Illustrator Creates Breathtaking, Solitary Worlds That Will Make You Want to Pause and Get Lost in Quiet Reflection
design.summary: Nishanul Nishat paints lone figures in vast, dreamlike landscapes, using soft color palettes and rich lighting to build atmospheric, narrative-driven scenes of quiet solitude.

marketing.title: PSA: Your brand already has an AI fingerprint
marketing.summary: You don't have to guess how AI interprets your brand. Markup AI's Free Brand Profile analyzes your publicly available content to articulate your voice, distinctive writing patterns, target personas, and preferred terminology. It then hands you a standard you can use to review content wherever you're already working. If you don't like what you see, you know what to change . Simply input your email and your company domain to get AI's view. No strings attached. Get your Free Brand Profile

marketing.title: Organic traffic is down, but it's not all AI
marketing.summary: Organic search traffic fell 13% in the US and 24% in France over two years, but losses vary by industry and site size. Publishers lost about 42% of organic traffic in both markets, while smaller sites remained roughly flat. Paid search traffic grew 21% in the US as larger ad blocks pushed organic results below the fold. AI referrals account for just 0.5% of total visits, suggesting that AI alone doesn't explain declining search traffic.

marketing.title: The End of the Internet
marketing.summary: The internet's shift from open blogs and social networks to algorithm-driven platforms has made discovery harder and independent businesses less sustainable. AI could accelerate this decline by flooding the web with content and creating more security risks. Smaller communities and businesses offer an alternative. Paid niche publications can thrive on loyal readers while private group chats build stronger connections. AI also makes it easier to create custom apps for individuals or small teams without needing mass-market demand.

marketing.title: Steal your competitor's customers for <$100
marketing.summary: Wispr Flow pays $35 for every paying Granola user who switches, covering their remaining subscription and adding 3 free months. The strategy recruits competitor affiliates by offering higher referral payouts. Existing customers can also refer contacts who use rivals, while sales teams can re-engage prospects who chose a competitor earlier in the year. Covering the remainder of their subscription reduces switching costs and gives them a reason to reconsider.

marketing.title: Influence is only as good as the rule behind it
marketing.summary: Influence can be a useful leading indicator when measured by engagement rather than impressions alone. An analysis of 1,000+ advertisers and $80 million in LinkedIn ad spend found that companies reached in 3 or more separate months entered the pipeline 1.5X more often. Those with 5 or more paid engagements entered 2.2X more often. Recent reach and engagement were stronger signals than longer lookback periods, supporting consistent advertising to future buyers.

marketing.title: A practical playbook for AI visibility and organic growth
marketing.summary: GrowthX turned thousands of hours running organic growth programs into one methodology: get your business context right, find the questions your buyers ask in search and AI, make every page earn its place and measure what's real. Get the free playbook

marketing.title: Pinterest unlocks premium inventory for programmatic buyers, scaling high-intent discovery
marketing.summary: Pinterest has made Programmatic Deals widely available in select markets, letting advertisers buy its video and display inventory through platforms like Amazon Ads and Google Display & Video 360. The move gives brands easier access to Pinterest's high-intent audience within existing media plans. The platform now reaches 640M monthly users.

marketing.title: Meet Claude, your new video editor
marketing.summary: A free kit of 30 Claude Code skills turns the model into a local video editor using ffmpeg and Python, with no paid APIs. It includes 18 motion effects and 12 editing tools that identify strong hooks from long recordings, cutting a 40-sec clip from a 60-min episode in 2 minutes. The tools also interpret spoken editing notes to select takes and refine cuts. Effects are designed for head-and-shoulders footage and take up to 5 minutes to render.

marketing.title: In a zero-click world, your best marketing doesn't show up in your analytics
marketing.summary: In a zero-click world, last-click attribution misses the content that builds trust long before a purchase. Tutorials and videos can influence buyers for years without getting credit for the sale. Talk directly to customers to learn what convinced them to buy and what keeps them loyal. Use AI to analyze their responses and uncover what your metrics miss.

marketing.title: LEGO and Daft Punk's team-up highlights exactly how brands should interact with fans
marketing.summary: LEGO built its Daft Punk collaboration around fan participation by turning a fan-designed set into a product after it won a LEGO Ideas contest and gained 10K supporters. It teased the partnership with a cryptic video that encouraged fans to decode and discuss the reveal. The launch film blended both brands' visual styles without letting either dominate. Rather than rush out products, LEGO treats the partnership as a long-term relationship with its audience.

marketing.title: Meta's Social Apps Are Growing. AI Recommendations Are Why.
marketing.summary: Feeds on Facebook, Instagram, and Threads now run more on AI predictions of what users want than on the accounts they follow.

marketing.title: How to structure B2B video ads
marketing.summary: A cheat sheet for structuring paid ads, launch videos, and customer ads.

founders.title: The Rise of the Self-Driving Company
founders.summary: Companies pay a lot to keep work moving between people, in meetings and status reports. At Replit, agents are taking on much of that. Designers now ship product changes themselves instead of handing ideas to engineers, and support uses agents to look into customer problems. Engineers wrote nearly three times as much code in the first half of 2026 while review times, rollbacks, and incidents held flat. At most companies, agents still run in chat windows and personal accounts with whatever logins someone handed them, and nobody can see what they did.

founders.title: Payments moats
founders.summary: As AI makes software easier to reproduce, defensibility increasingly rests in regulatory approvals, banking relationships, and accumulated operational knowledge. Records of agent decisions and human corrections can become an advantage that competitors cannot recreate simply by copying the product.

founders.title: The Simplest, Highest-ROI Place to Put an AI Agent Is Your Contact Me Form
founders.summary: Inbound qualification is a good place to start with agent deployments because the job is bounded. The agent just needs to answer questions, qualify, route, and book. There are clear success metrics: meetings booked and revenue closed. The downsides of implementing AI in inbound qualification are low because the alternative is a form that sits in a queue.

founders.title: Better AI didn't change how I work - humans did
founders.summary: One AI startup's head of product tried Claude Cowork in January, and it couldn't do the job. A month later, a newly hired product manager showed the head of product how he had Claude Code agents doing his work. Watching a direct report work that far ahead did more than any product demo. That month, the head of product built a first agent to draft the weekly update for leadership. By April, Cowork was running nine jobs. Keep a list of what AI can't do yet, and retry the top items every couple of months.

founders.title: Replit Monitoring Agent: Your very own software engineering team
founders.summary: Replit's Monitoring Agent is an on-call engineer for your published app. It watches for errors and slow responses, investigates each alert, tests a fix, and emails you a summary. It can also republish the fix on its own if you let it.

founders.title: Discover 1000+ services on Vercel Connect from the CLI
founders.summary: Vercel Connect CLI now lets users search over 1000 services directly from the terminal using filters like category or connection method. The update supports JSON formatting for scripts and agents, enhancing integration flexibility. Users need CLI version 64.1.0 or later to access these features.

founders.title: The full Claude Platform, available on Google Cloud
founders.summary: Startups can now spend their Google Cloud commitment on the full Claude Platform, which Anthropic runs and Google bills. Code execution, skills, and web search are included, and new features arrive the same day they do on Anthropic's own platform. Managed Agents and the MCP connector are in beta.

founders.title: Tokens Over Hires
founders.summary: Some startups now buy engineering in tokens instead of headcount. Two founders spend about $28,000 a year on AI, less than one engineer costs. In their first month, they merged 657 pull requests. Their biggest bill is about $1,500 a month for an AI code reviewer, so neither founder has to read every first draft. Their real limit is attention. While one founder was reviewing other work, a small database problem grew until it took the product down. So their next engineer will own one piece of the product, agents included.

founders.title: The forgotten industrialist
founders.summary: AI founders should use George F. Johnson's “Square Deal” framework: share productivity gains among employees, customers, and the business. That means giving employees meaningful ownership, passing savings on to customers, and reinvesting in growth. Lincoln Electric offers a proof point: the company pairs profit sharing with stock returns more than twice the S&P 500's since its 1995 IPO.

founders.title: The most advanced AI adopters now spend less on AI
founders.summary: Companies furthest along with AI are starting to spend less on it as cost controls tighten and models get cheaper.

founders.title: Let Chaos Reign, and Then Rein In Chaos
founders.summary: Some of the first office PCs were expensed as desks or typewriters to get past IT.

founders.title: Loving Ugly Babies
founders.summary: Most companies die in the long stretch before anyone cares, and that stretch is where most of the value gets built.

founders.title: When the Anecdotes Don't Match the Metrics
founders.summary: When customers complain but the dashboard looks fine, trust the customers, and fix what the dashboard measures.

crypto.title: SoFi Launches Tokenized Deposit That Earns 4.4% in Stablecoins
crypto.summary: SOFIE is the first consumer-facing tokenized deposit from a US nationally chartered bank, with each token representing $1 on deposit earning 4.40% APY under FDIC insurance. Members convert SOFIE one-to-one into SoFiUSD, which runs on Ethereum and Solana and settles SoFi's card program via Mastercard's network, connecting yield-bearing bank deposits to onchain rails. The product targets an estimated $64 billion in idle stablecoin capital (about 21% of the market) by adding yield and insurance protections that pure stablecoins lack. SOFIE is SoFi's fifth crypto product in under a year, following consumer token trading across 40+ assets and the SoFiUSD stablecoin launch, extending the bank's pattern of converting traditional financial primitives into onchain equivalents.

crypto.title: CoinDCX confirms $16 million loss from retired wallets
crypto.summary: CoinDCX admitted losing 15.99M USDT from deposit wallets it stopped using after its July 2025 hack, and says it absorbed the loss. It says an automated sweeping service failed for a period, so user deposits built up at a deprecated address with unknown vulnerabilities. FlashRescue's co-founder flagged the outflows on Wednesday. CEO Sumit Gupta called it “a false alarm,” and the company's account called the claims “misleading.” ZachXBT showed one address was used for 10 months after the 2025 incident and swept deposits as late as April and May 2026. He advised users to withdraw and said the founders either lied or were negligent. CoinDCX says user funds are safe in cold wallets, and trading and withdrawals continued. The July 2025 hack cost about $44M. The founders were also arrested in March over a fraud complaint.

crypto.title: Circle Launches Circle Match for Institutional Users
crypto.summary: Circle Match, available for eligible Circle Mint customers, is an hourly auction that pairs institutional USDC mint and redemption orders within the Mint platform. When orders clear, minting participants receive a rebate while redemptions settle at a price the redeemer sets, distributing economic incentives to both sides of the institutional mint-redeem cycle. The underlying USDC flows remain unchanged, with Circle layering a price-discovery and rebate mechanism on top of existing infrastructure rather than altering the asset or its peg mechanics.

crypto.title: Vulnerabilities Found in Glamsterdam, Agents Came to the Rescue
crypto.summary: ChainSecurity flagged vulnerabilities in EIP-8037/8038, two state-pricing EIPs central to Glamsterdam's planned gas limit increase from 60M to 200M, with at least 13 major DeFi protocols identified as affected. The mechanism: EIP-8037's gas refill when storage slots are freed breaks the 1/64 gas guarantee in nested contract calls, enabling attackers to trigger outer-contract error handlers that lacked the gas to execute under the prior pricing model. Researchers from the Ethereum Foundation and Ethlabs each deployed AI agents overnight to scan for vulnerable contracts, then merged their efforts into a shared GitHub coordination repo where agents claim tasks via issue comments, deposit findings in structured directories, and produce consolidated memos without human intermediation. Core devs at the ACD paused any Glamsterdam launch date pending full impact analysis. The same agent-scanning framework is now running against EIP-8198 (Quick Slots, 12s to 10s slot time) ahead of Hegotá.

crypto.title: This Week on Base: Meme Summit, Mastercard, and More
crypto.summary: Mastercard launched Agent Pay for Machines with Cloudflare on Base, enabling AI agents to pay for digital services via x402. Morpho Midnight crossed $100M in total deposits, while Mag 7 tokenized stockholders deposited $9.57M and borrowed $4.08M USDC on Aave, with three in four of those users new to the protocol. Coinbase and The Block research puts the cost of a $200 USDC transfer on Base at 86% below traditional services. The week's launch slate included Thunes integrating stablecoins across its global payout network, Frax adding onchain FX markets, heydotxyz listing 194 tokenized stocks, and Spark Finance supplying over $400M USDC to Morpho's cbBTC/USDC market.

crypto.title: Perps Will Eat Options
crypto.summary: On-chain options hold under 1% of perp DEX volume despite representing 3x futures volume in TradFi. The gap persists partly because 10x perp positions carry a 47% liquidation probability over 180 days, making options the structurally superior instrument for multi-week theses. The growth mechanism is reflexive: options sellers hedge on perp markets, expanding perp OI rather than cannibalizing it, a dynamic Deribit already demonstrates with $2B+ in futures OI sourced from options hedging. September posted the best on-chain options month on record at ~$5B notional (7% of Deribit volume), with Derive commanding 90%+ of on-chain premium at $18B notional traded and DRV up 1,000%+ YTD at 66x annualized revenue. On-chain options are projected to grow from 0.8% to 5% of perp volume. Hyperliquid via Hypercall's shared margin, Derive, and Paradex will be the primary beneficiaries.

crypto.title: Keystone Hardware Wallet Confirms Customer Shipping Data Breach
crypto.summary: Keystone Hardware Wallet confirmed on October 23 that a third party accessed customer shipping data through its website, exposing names, addresses, contact details, and order information, while payment credentials, recovery phrases, private keys, and wallet passwords remained unaffected. The breach was detected on October 20 and traced through Shopify API logs. Keystone has blocked the access, patched the vulnerability, and opened a formal investigation with customer notifications underway. Keystone warns affected users to expect phishing attempts from actors impersonating the company offering refunds or replacement devices, and urges customers never to share recovery phrases and to navigate to the site directly rather than clicking unsolicited links.

crypto.title: Crypto apps worth trying this week
crypto.summary: This post presents a roundup of new apps, framed around Solana's 150 ms finality, Hyperliquid tooling, and growing tokenized stock DeFi. Hypurrdash is a Hyperliquid terminal with private TWAPs, swarm orders, a liquidation heatmap, and new VWAP orders. Silhouette turned on perps RFQ for BTC and HYPE, up to $100k per quote. 2Factor Finance offers about 1.33x BTC on Base with no liquidation price. Trueo has permissionless prediction markets where positions earn yield in a Yearn USDC vault. Catalyst runs perps on whether an event happens. Pabox lets you borrow USDG against Robinhood Stock Tokens, pausing when the stock market is closed. Fluxion is Mantle's native DEX for xStocks 24/7.

crypto.summary: US hourly wages are up about 1,200% since 1964 against about 10,000% for the S&P 500.

crypto.summary: Zeneca says he now asks an AI agent to “do a deep dive on [XYZ]” and shares the seven things he first asked for.

it.summary: AI is creating a new ceiling for service management - and expectations are catching up quickly. Customers and employees want seamless support. Service teams have to resolve issues faster and more proactively. It's a high bar to meet. But the best IT service desks are riding this wave to deliver massive value. it.title: Anthropic's soaring sales, steep losses put AI frenzy to IPO test
it.summary: Anthropic published its US IPO filing as investors scrutinize the cost of the AI boom. Its first-half net loss was $80.7 billion, largely driven by a non-operating convertible-bond item, while its operating loss narrowed to $693 million. The prospectus also highlights growing computing costs and dependence on a small group of cloud and chip suppliers.

it.title: Microsoft finally brings a unified inbox to new Outlook for Windows
it.summary: New Outlook for Windows is rolling out an All Accounts view that brings email from multiple connected accounts into one place while keeping each mailbox separate. Microsoft expects rollout to finish by late October, with administrator controls planned separately.

it.title: Gheist: Attempted Scaled Abuse of Stolen GitHub Tokens Stumbles
it.summary: A campaign tracked by Wiz uses stolen GitHub tokens to plant workflows that steal repository secrets and can expose cloud credentials. GitHub's approval controls blocked every malicious public-repository run the researchers checked, but Wiz observed successful runs and follow-on cloud activity involving private repositories and enterprise environments. The report includes indicators for investigating affected accounts and guidance on revoking tokens and rotating exposed secrets.

it.title: The metric that makes your IT org look healthier than it is
it.summary: Strong uptime, ticket-resolution, and patch-compliance percentages can hide recurring problems and risks concentrated in a few critical systems. Executive reporting should emphasize business disruption, repeat incidents, and unresolved critical vulnerabilities, while retaining operational metrics for the teams that use them.

it.title: Azure Communication Services is retiring: now what
it.summary: Microsoft has announced the retirement of most Azure Communication Services (ACS) features by September 30, 2028, limiting ongoing functionality exclusively to Microsoft Teams integrations. New customer onboarding was restricted starting in late 2026, and existing standalone services such as chat, SMS, and WhatsApp will be shut down entirely. This move suggests Microsoft's failure to capture a viable standalone market, leaving enterprise users facing a difficult migration.

it.title: Cognitive Mercantilism
it.summary: Contemporary AI fears reflect a form of cognitive mercantilism, which treats intelligence as a scarce resource and underestimates ordinary people's ability to think independently. Much like the consumer revolution that preceded industrial capitalism, widespread access to AI could spark a cognitive industrious revolution. Abundant AI could expand demand for intelligence and empower ordinary people to access and apply it on an unprecedented scale.

it.title: Reach 8 million tech professionals reading TLDR
it.summary: Ads get ignored on social media but not in TLDR! Reach IT pros and IT leaders where they actually pay attention. Learn more about sponsorship opportunities .

it.title: AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN now support 1:1 NAT
it.summary: AWS now provides managed one-to-one network address translation directly on AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN attachments through integration with Regional Private NAT Gateway. This capability enables customers to connect private networks sharing the same IP address ranges without renumbering networks, deploying NAT appliances, or writing return-traffic rules. The service automatically applies address translation in both directions across Amazon VPC, AWS Site-to-Site VPN, AWS Direct Connect, and connected SD-WAN appliances.

it.title: Wireless is the next security frontier, and Cisco is leading the way
it.summary: Cisco is launching the CW9176ISEC, described as the industry's first Wi-Fi 7 access point with quantum-resilient capabilities aligned to CNSA 2.0 standards. The company is also refreshing its Wireless 9800 Series controllers and introducing Auto MACsec to secure traffic between access points and switches. In partnership with Qualcomm, Microsoft, and Intel, Cisco is bringing post-quantum cryptography over the air to protect enterprise wireless infrastructure and client devices.

it.title: Consumer Agents Sitting Inside Enterprise SaaS
it.summary: Threat research has flagged a surge of consumer personal agents connecting directly to core enterprise SaaS suites without corporate IT oversight. C-level executives are granting these unvetted third-party agents expansive OAuth privileges, creating unmonitored non-human identities with access to sensitive corporate data and files. Legacy security architectures are blind to these cloud-to-cloud connections, necessitating active, context-aware SaaS and non-human identity governance.

it.title: How We Gave AI Agents the Keys to Production and Still Sleep at Night
it.summary: monday.com's Production Engineering team built a shared platform that allows LLM agents to safely interact with production infrastructure through standardized guardrails. After one quarter in production, agents resolved about 50 percent of an average of 1,688 infrastructure tickets per month without human escalation.

it.title: US Army launches Project Gatekeeper to accelerate commercial software adoption, streamline cybersecurity accreditation
it.summary: The Army's new software-testing sandbox produces evidence to support security authorization.

it.title: Dayforce to Acquire Ribbon AI Inc. to Advance Agentic Recruiting
it.summary: The acquisition will bring Ribbon's conversational voice and video AI technology, sourcing, and talent rediscovery tools to Dayforce to help organizations automate early-stage screening and conduct interviews at scale.
